1883magazine.justification: London-based fashion and culture magazine whose theatre coverage is occasional (5 London reviews since 2023). Kept at the default tier; no clear reason to move.

2ontheaisle.justification: Small WordPress theatre blog that covered Broadway in 2015-2017 and is now inactive. Kept at current tier as no evidence it ranks lower or higher.

4columns.justification: Online arts criticism magazine with established freelance critics, covering New York theatre occasionally (11 reviews). A small but edited outlet, which fits T3.

a-youngish-perspective.justification: UK theatre review blog active since 2025 with steady London volume (38 reviews). Smaller semi-pro outlet; kept at T3.

aaron-in-nyc.justification: Small New York theatre blog with a handful of reviews since 2025. Kept at current tier; volume is low but not by itself grounds to demote.

about-entertainment.justification: Defunct theatre section of About.com (theater.about.com), closed around 2016-2017. Kept at the tier that reflected its standing while publishing.

act-three-the-reviews.justification: Single-author Blogspot theatre blog (Doug Marino) active 2016-2017, now inactive. Kept at current tier.

adriandimanlig.justification: Personal theatre review site active 2017-2019, now inactive. Kept at current tier.

adventuresintheatreland.justification: UK theatre blog that began reviewing London shows in August 2026 (11 reviews). Too new to judge a move; kept at current tier.

afridiziak-theatre-news.justification: Long-running London site covering Black British theatre, with regular London reviews since 2024 (26). Niche specialist outlet; kept at current tier.

albany-times-union.justification: Regional daily newspaper in Albany, NY, reviewing a few Broadway or touring productions. Local paper fits T3.

all-that-dazzles-uk.justification: UK theatre review site with heavy, sustained London volume since 2021 (141 London reviews). Semi-pro specialist site; kept at T3.

america-magazine.justification: Jesuit weekly magazine whose theatre coverage is incidental (4 reviews over seven years). Kept at T4.

amny.justification: amNewYork, a free New York daily with a long-serving theatre critic (Matt Windman) and sustained volume (370 reviews since 2009). Fits T2 as an established local daily.

another-eye-opens.justification: Substack newsletter by veteran critic Don Shewey with a single review in the corpus. Kept at current tier.

ap.justification: Associated Press, the national wire service whose Broadway reviews are syndicated across US papers; long-running presence (222 NYC reviews). Kept at nyc1; London tier unchanged as it does not review there.

around-the-town-chicago.justification: Small Chicago-area arts site reviewing touring productions (5 reviews). Kept at current tier.

artsdesk.justification: The Arts Desk, a UK arts site staffed by former national-newspaper critics, with steady London volume (120 reviews). Matches the T2 anchor list.

artsfuse.justification: The Arts Fuse, a Boston-based edited arts magazine with occasional New York coverage (17 reviews). Fits T3.

as-her-world-turns.justification: Personal theatre blog active 2015-2016, now inactive. Kept at current tier.

attitude.justification: UK LGBTQ lifestyle magazine with incidental theatre coverage (3 London reviews). Kept at T4.

av-club.justification: The A.V. Club, a film and TV site whose theatre coverage is incidental (3 reviews). Kept at T4.

bachtrack.justification: Bachtrack, an international classical music, opera and dance review site with occasional theatre reviews in both markets (11). Kept at T3.

backstage.justification: Backstage, the long-running trade publication for performers, which ran regular reviews until 2013 (93 reviews). Defunct as a review source; keeps the T2 tier that reflected its standing.

backstage-barbie.justification: Single-author Blogspot theatre blog active 2015-2017, now inactive. Kept at current tier.

billboard.justification: Billboard, a major music trade publication whose theatre reviews are incidental (5 over seven years). Kept at current tier; low volume alone is not grounds to demote.

blogcritics.justification: Blogcritics, a multi-contributor culture blog network with occasional theatre reviews (15). Fits T3.

bloomberg.justification: Bloomberg News ran regular theatre criticism (Jeremy Gerard, John Simon) until 2018; inactive since. Defunct as a theatre source; keeps the T2 tier from when it published.

bobs-theater-blog.justification: Single-author theatre blog active 2015-2017, now inactive. Kept at current tier.

boston-com.justification: Boston.com, the Boston Globe's free sister site, with a few reviews (5). Kept at T3.

boston-globe.justification: The Boston Globe, a major regional daily, reviewing pre-Broadway and touring productions occasionally (17). Kept at T3 given incidental NYC coverage.

british-theatre.justification: Keep T2 for now, but this id needs splitting before any tier call: 48 of its 98 rows link to British Theatre Guide (britishtheatreguide.info, a long-running UK review site with established critics), 9 to BritishTheatre.com (a smaller news and review site) and 41 have no URL. A T3 demotion was considered for BritishTheatre.com but would also hit the British Theatre Guide rows.

broadway-and-me.justification: Broadway & Me, a single-author blog by Jan Simpson with sustained volume since 2015 (44 reviews). Kept at current tier.

broadway-blog.justification: Keep T2. The Broadway Blog is a NYC theatre site associated with Matthew Wexler. A T3 move was considered (it may be inactive; the site returned 503 and no 2026 posts were found) but its editorial model could not be verified, and defunct outlets keep the tier they held while publishing.

broadway-journal.justification: Small theatre review site active 2018-2019, now inactive. Kept at current tier.

broadway-showbiz.justification: Small theatre blog active 2015-2017, now inactive. Kept at current tier.

broadwaynews.justification: Broadway News (Broadway News, Inc.) is an active Broadway trade news site. Charles Isherwood reviewed for it from its 2017 launch until he became the Wall Street Journal critic in 2022; his 78 reviews here stay T1 either way because he is on the top-critics list. The other 136 reviews (mostly Brittani Samuel) are trade-site criticism comparable to TheaterMania, so propose NYC 1 to 2.

broadwayselect.justification: Small Broadway blog active 2015-2019, now inactive. Kept at current tier.

broadwayworld.justification: BroadwayWorld, the largest theatre news site with staff and contributor reviewers in both markets and the highest volume in the corpus (503). Kept at T2 in both markets.

bsonarts.justification: Personal arts blog active 2017-2018, now inactive. Kept at current tier.

buffalorising.justification: Buffalo Rising, a local Buffalo, NY community news site reviewing touring productions (5). Kept at current tier.

cabaret-scenes.justification: Cabaret Scenes, a cabaret-focused magazine with occasional theatre reviews (17). Niche specialist outlet; kept at T3.

carey-purcell.justification: Freelance theatre writer Carey Purcell with 6 reviews in 2016-2017 and no outlet domain recorded. Unclear what outlet carried these; kept at current tier.

center-on-the-aisle.justification: Small theatre review site active 2015-2018, now inactive. Kept at current tier.

chelsea-community-news.justification: Hyperlocal Manhattan community news site with incidental theatre coverage (10 reviews). Kept at T4.

chicago-reader.justification: Chicago Reader, an established alt-weekly, reviewing touring productions occasionally (7). Fits T3 for NYC-market coverage.

chicago-sun-times.justification: Chicago Sun-Times, a major big-city daily with a staff critic, reviewing pre-Broadway and touring productions (15). Kept at T2 as a major daily.

chicagotribune.justification: Chicago Tribune, whose long-serving critic Chris Jones is one of the most read US theatre critics, with sustained volume (311 reviews). Kept at T2.

cititour.justification: Cititour, a New York arts site whose reviews are written by veteran critic Brian Scott Lipton, with sustained volume since 2014 (292). Kept at T2.

city-am.justification: City A.M., a free London business daily with a regular theatre critic, steady since 2023 (29 London reviews). Kept at T3.

city-cabaret.justification: Cabaret and theatre review site active 2016-2019, now inactive. Kept at current tier.

cleveland-plain-dealer.justification: The Cleveland Plain Dealer, a regional daily, reviewing touring productions (10). Kept at T3.

clevescene.justification: Cleveland Scene, a local alt-weekly, reviewing touring productions (5). Kept at T3.

cote-notices.justification: Substack newsletter by David Cote, a long-established New York critic (formerly Time Out New York), active since 2026 (8 reviews). Kept at T3.

cultural-capital.justification: Personal WordPress blog (Maryam Philpott) reviewing London shows since August 2026 (5). Kept at current tier.

culturesauce.justification: Culture Sauce, a small site run by veteran critic Thom Geier (formerly Entertainment Weekly), with strong recent volume (170 reviews). Kept at T3.

curtain-call-reviews.justification: Small UK review blog with few London reviews (4). Kept at T4.

curtainup.justification: CurtainUp, a long-running online theatre magazine with a stable of critics, defunct since 2020 after 129 reviews. Keeps the T2 tier from when it published.

daily-mail.justification: Daily Mail, a national UK tabloid with a staff critic (Patrick Marmion) and sustained London volume (143 reviews). The tier brief lists the Daily Mail among T2 London outlets, below the Guardian, Times and Telegraph, so lon1 is out of line. Considered a London move to T2 (mass-market tabloid next to the broadsheets at T1), not proposed: the evidence was the audit rubric, not the outlet. Owner call.

dailybeast.justification: The Daily Beast, a national news site with a regular theatre critic (Tim Teeman) and sustained volume (253). Kept at T2.

dallasvoice.justification: Dallas Voice, a regional LGBTQ weekly reviewing touring productions (6). Kept at T3.

dc-metro-theater-arts.justification: DC Metro Theater Arts, a Washington-area multi-contributor theatre site with an editor (active here 2015-2019). Kept at T3.

dc-theater-arts.justification: DC Theater Arts (dctheaterarts.org) is the renamed DC Metro Theater Arts, founded 2012 and run as the nonprofit Metro Theater Arts with an editor-in-chief. Its old id dc-metro-theater-arts is T3, so propose 4 to 3 so the two ids match.

dctheatrescene.justification: DC Theatre Scene, a Washington-area theatre site whose New York reviews came largely from Jonathan Mandell, with high volume 2015-2020. Kept at current tier.

deadline.justification: Deadline, a major entertainment trade publication with a staff Broadway critic, high sustained volume (318). Kept at nyc1/lon2.

diandra-reviews-it-all.justification: Personal review blog active 2017-2018, now inactive. Kept at current tier.

digital-journal.justification: Digital Journal, a contributor-driven news site whose theatre coverage is incidental (27 reviews). Kept at T4.

digital-spy.justification: Digital Spy, a UK entertainment site with no reviews in the corpus. Kept at current tier.

drama-queen-nyc.justification: Small New York theatre blog active 2015-2019, now inactive. Kept at current tier.

dread-central.justification: Dread Central, a horror film site with incidental theatre coverage (2 reviews). Kept at T4.

dtli.justification: Did They Like It (didtheylikeit.com) is a review aggregator, not an outlet. All 40 rows link to didtheylikeit.com, so they are aggregator pages filed under a fake outlet and should be reattributed to the original critics. Tier kept at current until then.

edge-new-york.justification: EDGE Media Network's New York edition, an LGBTQ news site with a single-day batch of reviews in 2017. Kept at current tier.

epoch-times.justification: The Epoch Times, a national newspaper with regular theatre reviews in 2015-2017 (19). Kept at T3.

everything-theatre.justification: Everything Theatre describes itself as a 100% volunteer-run collective (founded 2011 as a two-person blog, now 60+ volunteers with volunteer editors), mostly covering London fringe and Off-West End. That editorial model fits T3, not the professional T2 outlets; propose London 2 to 3.

ew.justification: Entertainment Weekly, a national entertainment magazine with sustained theatre coverage (435 reviews). Kept at T2.

exeunt-magazine.justification: Exeunt NYC is a multi-contributor critical theatre magazine with an editor and longform reviews of Broadway and Off-Broadway, active for a decade with steady volume. Its standing as a recognized specialist outlet fits T2.

express-uk.justification: The Daily Express is a UK national daily whose theatre reviews have come from professional critics such as Neil Norman (most recent found October 2024). A national daily fits T3 better than the T4 blog floor; propose London 4 to 3. It does not review NYC shows.

fairypoweredproductions.justification: Appears to be a small London blog with 8 reviews since July 2026 and no recognized-critic status. Keep T4.

faster-times.justification: Defunct online magazine (2010-2011) with only 5 NYC reviews; a small multi-contributor site. Keep T3 as it stood when publishing.

film-festival-traveler.justification: Small film-focused site whose theatre coverage was occasional (11 NYC reviews, 2015-2017, now inactive). Keep T3.

financialtimes.justification: The Financial Times is a major international paper; in London its staff critics (Sarah Hemming and others) are among the critics who set the market, while its NYC coverage is a respected but secondary voice. The existing NYC T2 / London T1 split reflects that and it reviews in both markets.

firstnightmagazine.justification: A newer London theatre magazine site with 23 reviews since December 2025; a small specialist outlet. Keep T3.

flicker-magazine.justification: A small arts magazine with 7 London reviews since late 2025. Keep T3.

flipsidereviews.justification: Single-author Blogspot blog with 5 NYC reviews in 2015-2016, likely picked up via an aggregator (Show Score) at the time; inactive since. Low volume alone does not justify a move, keep T3.

fordham-observer.justification: Fordham University's Lincoln Center student newspaper, 8 NYC reviews in 2017-2018, now inactive. A student paper is at the low end of T3 but with aggregator-era pickup it stays at T3.

fort-worth-star-telegram.justification: A regional Texas daily with professional staff; only 3 NYC reviews (November 2025). Keep T3 as a regional paper.

forward.justification: The Forward is an established Jewish news publication whose theatre coverage is occasional (14 NYC reviews over 14 years). Theatre is incidental to its mission, which fits the current T4.

fringereview.justification: FringeReview is a UK multi-reviewer site covering fringe and London theatre, active with 18 London reviews since 2025. Keep T3.

front-row-center.justification: Front Row Center is a long-running NYC theatre review site with 368 reviews since 2013 and sustained per-year share (normPct 2.3). It is a regular critical voice, keep T2.

frontmezzjunkies.justification: Front Mezz Junkies is a single-editor NYC theatre site with aggregator pickup and 119 reviews since 2015. Keep T3.

gizmodo.justification: Tech and culture site with a single NYC theatre review; theatre coverage is incidental. Keep T4.

gotham-playgoer.justification: Gotham Playgoer was a single-author Blogspot theatre blog with 32 NYC reviews (2015-2019) that appeared in aggregator coverage at the time; now inactive. Keep T3.

guardian.justification: The Guardian is a major international paper; its London critics (Arifa Akbar and others) set the market and its US theatre coverage (Alexis Soloski and others) is a regular NYC voice with 252 NYC reviews. Keep T1 in both markets.

hampstead-highgate-express.justification: The Ham&High is a long-standing North London local paper with a theatre critic, 19 London reviews since 2023. Keep T3 as a local paper.

harry-theatre-life.justification: Appears to be a small London theatre blog with 5 reviews since June 2026. Keep current T3; not enough information to justify a move.

hartford-courant.justification: The Hartford Courant is an established Connecticut daily with a professional theatre critic; 14 NYC reviews. Keep T3 as a regional paper.

hollywood-reporter.justification: The Hollywood Reporter is a major entertainment trade whose chief theatre critic (David Rooney) is one of the market-setting NYC voices, with 403 NYC reviews. Its London coverage is minimal (4 reviews), so the existing NYC T1 / London T2 split stands.

hollywood-soapbox.justification: Small entertainment blog with 3 NYC reviews (2024-2025). Keep T4.

huffpost.justification: HuffPost carried NYC theatre reviews by known critics through its contributor platform (145 reviews, heavy in 2015-2019); theatre coverage has essentially stopped since 2022. Keep T2 as the tier that reflected its standing when it published.

i-paper.justification: The i is a UK national daily whose theatre critics are regulars in London review coverage (46 London reviews, rising since 2022). The existing London T1 / NYC T2 split stands; it does not review NYC shows.

independent.justification: The Independent is a UK national with established theatre critics, a regular London voice (72 London reviews) and an occasional NYC reviewer (13). Keep NYC T2 / London T1.

indiewire.justification: IndieWire is an established film and TV trade with professional staff; only 2 NYC theatre reviews (2018-2021). Low volume alone does not justify a demotion, keep T2.

jitney.justification: The Jitney (jitneybooks.com) appears to be a small literary/Hamptons outlet with 2 NYC reviews on one date. Keep T4.

jks-theatre-scene.justification: JK's Theatre Scene is a single-author NYC theatre blog with 11 reviews, mostly before 2020. Keep T4.

jonathan-baz.justification: Jonathan Baz runs a single-author London theatre review blog known in fringe circles; 17 London reviews, all dated to one day, suggesting a bulk import. Keep T3.

josh-at-the-movies.justification: Josh at the Movies is a single-author film blog with occasional NYC theatre reviews (12 since 2022). Keep T4.

journal-inquirer.justification: The Journal Inquirer is a small Connecticut daily newspaper; 5 NYC reviews in 2018. Keep T3 as a local paper.

la-voce-di-new-york.justification: La Voce di New York is an Italian-language New York news site with editorial staff, 27 NYC reviews since 2025. Keep T3.

labor-press.justification: LaborPress is a New York labor-news site with occasional theatre reviews (12, 2016-2018), now inactive for theatre. Keep T3.

latimes.justification: The Los Angeles Times is a major national paper whose chief theatre critic (Charles McNulty) reviews notable NYC productions; 84 NYC reviews. Keep T1; it does not review London shows.

lbc.justification: LBC is a UK talk-radio station whose website ran 2 London theatre pieces; theatre is incidental to it. Keep T4.

li-herald.justification: The Long Island Herald is a community weekly; 5 NYC reviews in 2017. Keep T3 as a local paper.

liamodell.justification: Liam O'Dell is a freelance journalist whose own site carries 34 London reviews since 2025; single-author but a working journalist rather than a hobby blogger. Keep T3.

lighting-and-sound-america.justification: Lighting & Sound America is a professional theatre-technology trade magazine whose editors review NYC productions with design focus; 218 NYC reviews since 2015 with steady presence. Keep T2.

london-box-office.justification: London Box Office is a ticket seller that also publishes reviews and appears as an aggregator source in this project's pipeline, so some rows may be misattributed aggregator data rather than its own criticism. Flagged for review; keep current T2.

london-theatre.justification: LondonTheatre.co.uk is a long-running London theatre news and reviews site with a roster of named critics, 166 London reviews concentrated since 2022. Keep T2.

london-theatre-reviews.justification: London Theatre Reviews is a multi-contributor London review site, 24 reviews since 2022. Keep T3.

london-unattached.justification: London Unattached is a London lifestyle blog with occasional theatre reviews (34 since 2025) and no recognized-critic status. Keep T4.

londonist.justification: Londonist is a London city-guide site whose theatre coverage is incidental (4 reviews). Keep T4.

londonlivinglarge.justification: London Living Large appears to be a London lifestyle blog with 10 theatre reviews since August 2026. Keep T3; not enough information to justify a move.

londonpubtheatres.justification: London Pub Theatres is a fringe-focused London magazine site with 15 reviews since 2026. Keep T3.

londontheatre1.justification: LondonTheatre1 is a long-running multi-reviewer London theatre site with 125 London reviews, mostly since 2022. Keep T2.

londontheatredirect.justification: London Theatre Direct is a ticket-selling site that also runs editorial reviews; 16 London reviews. Commercial ownership argues against promotion, keep T3.

lost-in-theatreland.justification: Lost in Theatreland is a small London theatre blog with 5 reviews. Keep T4.

loureviews.justification: LouReviews appears to be a single-author London review blog with 60 reviews since 2025 and a sizeable recent share. Keep T3.

luxury-experience.justification: Lifestyle site with a single NYC theatre review; theatre is incidental. Keep T4.

magical-misstari-tour.justification: Single-author Blogspot blog with 7 NYC reviews (2016-2018), likely aggregator pickup at the time; inactive. Keep T3.

maryland-theatre-guide.justification: Maryland Theatre Guide is a regional multi-contributor theatre site with occasional NYC reviews (12 since 2024). Keep T3.

mashable.justification: Mashable is a large digital media site with professional staff; theatre coverage is occasional (17 NYC reviews). Keep T3.

matineemouse.justification: Matinee Mouse is a single-author Substack with 6 London reviews. Keep T4.

medium.justification: Medium is a self-publishing blogging platform, not an outlet; the 20 NYC reviews are individual writers' posts with no editorial oversight. That matches the T4 definition of single-author blogs rather than T3.

melindas-malarky.justification: Single-author Blogspot blog with 11 NYC reviews (2018-2019), likely aggregator pickup at the time; inactive. Keep T3.

metrmag.justification: Small outlet with 6 NYC reviews in 2026; I could not confirm what it is. Keep current T3.

metro-uk.justification: Metro is a UK national free daily with professional staff; occasional London theatre reviews (9). Keep T3.

minneapolis-star-tribune.justification: The Star Tribune is a major Midwest regional daily with a professional critic; 5 NYC reviews. Keep T3 as a regional paper.

monstagigz.justification: Monstagigz appears to be a small UK music and theatre review blog with 24 London reviews since late 2025. Keep T3; not enough information to justify a move.

musical-theatre-review.justification: Musical Theatre Review is an established UK specialist site with named critics, 66 reviews across both markets (2015-2021) and inactive since. Keep T3 as it stood when publishing.

national-review.justification: National Review is a national political magazine whose theatre reviews were occasional (6, 2018-2019). Keep T3.

nbcny.justification: NBC New York (Robert Kahn) reviewed Broadway regularly from 2013 to 2017 with 128 reviews and a high per-year share; its theatre coverage is now defunct. Keep T2 as it stood when publishing.

new-city-stage.justification: New City Stage is a small NYC theatre site with 9 reviews since 2022. Keep T3.

new-jersey-newsroom.justification: NJ Newsroom was a New Jersey news site with a regular theatre reviewer (62 NYC reviews, 2009-2015); theatre coverage is defunct. Keep T3.

new-york-classical-review.justification: New York Classical Review is a professional music criticism site with established critics, reviewing opera and music theatre in NYC (21 since 2024). Keep T3.

new-york-notebook.justification: New York Notebook is a Substack with 6 NYC reviews since 2025. Keep current T3; not enough information to justify a move.

new-york-sun.justification: The New York Sun (relaunched online) has a regular NYC theatre critic with 118 reviews since 2022 and a solid per-year share. Keep T2.

newnownextcom.justification: NewNowNext was Logo TV's LGBTQ entertainment site with occasional theatre reviews (10, 2017-2019); defunct. Keep T3.

newsday.justification: Newsday's Linda Winer was one of the market-setting NYC critics for decades (366 reviews, highest normPct in this batch) until coverage ended in 2019; defunct for theatre reviews. Keep NYC T1 as it stood when publishing.

newsweek.justification: Newsweek is a national news magazine with occasional theatre reviews (11, 2016-2022). Keep T3.

newyorker.justification: The New Yorker is a market-setting NYC publication with staff critics (Vinson Cunningham, Helen Shaw); 116 NYC reviews. Keep NYC T1; it does not review London shows.

njarts.justification: NJArts.net is a New Jersey arts site run by a veteran journalist with contributors; 5 NYC reviews. Keep T3.

njcom.justification: NJ.com carries the Star-Ledger's theatre criticism, a long-standing professional daily critic with 82 NYC reviews (mostly before 2020). Keep T2.

north-west-end.justification: Regional UK theatre review site with a team of volunteer reviewers covering the North West and some London shows. Recent entrant (2026) with modest volume; the current T3 fits.

northjerseycom.justification: Website of The Record and other North Jersey daily papers, whose staff theatre critics (for example Robert Feldberg) reviewed Broadway for decades. Coverage has faded since 2022, but its standing as an established daily supports keeping T2.

ny1.justification: New York cable news channel whose theatre critic Roma Torre was a recognized Broadway reviewer and a strong regular presence in 2015-2019. Theatre reviews stopped in 2020 (defunct as a review source); keep the tier that reflected its standing.

nyc-theatre-addict.justification: Appears to be a small personal theatre blog with only 5 reviews across nine years. Kept at the current T3 since there is no evidence to justify a move either way.

nydailynews.justification: Major New York daily with long-serving staff critics (Joe Dziemianowicz and others), steady volume over decades. Matches T2.

nypost.justification: Major New York daily with a staff theatre critic (Johnny Oleksinski), steady presence in both periods. Matches T2.

nysr.justification: New York Stage Review, founded 2018 by veteran critics from the major dailies (Frank Scheck, David Finkle, Steven Suskin and others), one of the highest-volume voices in the 2022+ corpus. Matches T2.

nyt-theater.justification: New York Theater, Jonathan Mandell's long-running site; largely single-author but by a veteran journalist, picked up by aggregators and very consistent in volume since 2010. Keep T2.

nytg.justification: New York Theatre Guide, an established theatre-specialist site with a roster of regular critics and strong 2022+ volume. Matches T2.

nytheatre.justification: nytheatre.com (Martin Denton's long-running Off-Broadway review site, later nytheatre-wire); defunct, last review 2017. Keep the T3 it held while active.

nytimes.justification: The New York Times, the paper of record whose critics set the Broadway verdict; its London reviews are occasional and carry less market weight there. Keep the nyc1/lon2 split.

observer.justification: In NYC this is the New York Observer (observer.com), a recognized arts outlet that fits T2. The London rows reflect The Observer (UK Sunday paper), which the tier guide places in T2 alongside the Independent and Daily Mail, so lon1 overstates it relative to the daily nationals that set the London verdict. Considered a London move to T2 (The Observer changed ownership in 2025 and its long-time critic retired), not proposed for lack of sourced evidence. Note: this id appears to hold both the New York Observer (NYC rows) and the UK Observer (London rows).

oc-register.justification: Orange County Register, a regional California daily reviewing touring productions; small NYC-show volume. Matches T3 as a regional paper.

off-off-online.justification: OffOffOnline is a long-running multi-contributor site focused on Off-Off-Broadway, with growing 2022+ volume. It could argue for T3, but its scope is fringe-focused and the current T4 is defensible; keep.

off-script-with-dan-dwyer.justification: Small personal review site active only 2018-2019 (defunct). Keep current T3; too little evidence for a move.

on-off-broadway.justification: Small site with 15 reviews all dated to a single day in 2010, likely a bulk import or index page rather than a sustained outlet. Keep current T3.

onandoffbroadwaytheaterreviews.justification: Small theatre review blog active 2018-2019, now apparently inactive. Keep current T3.

one-minute-critic.justification: 1 Minute Critic, a short-form review outlet with high 2025-2026 volume covering Broadway and Off-Broadway. Keep T3.

onin.justification: Unable to confirm what onin.london is beyond a small London review site with 7 reviews since May 2026. Keep current tier.

operawire.justification: OperaWire, a multi-contributor opera news and review site whose theatre coverage overlaps only on opera-adjacent shows. Keep T3.

out-magazine.justification: Out, a national LGBTQ magazine with occasional theatre reviews; no theatre reviews in the corpus since 2019. Keep T3.

pages-on-stages.justification: Pages on Stages, a regular NYC theatre-specialist site with 129 reviews since 2021. Matches T3.

parade.justification: Parade magazine, a national Sunday supplement; theatre reviews are incidental (5 in 2018). Kept at T2 per the default-keep rule, though it is a candidate for review if more data appears.

parterre-box.justification: Parterre Box, a long-established opera site with an editor and multiple contributors; theatre reviews are occasional. Keep T3.

partially-obstructed-view.justification: Partially Obstructed View, a long-running London theatre blog by a single author. Low volume in the corpus; keep current T3.

peconic-public-broadcasting.justification: Peconic Public Broadcasting (WPPB, Long Island public radio) ran theatre reviews 2015-2018 (defunct in the corpus). Keep T3 as a small regional outlet.

people.justification: People magazine, a national entertainment weekly with occasional theatre reviews and very low volume. Kept at T2 per the default-keep rule.

philadelphia-inquirer.justification: The Philadelphia Inquirer, a major metropolitan daily whose critics occasionally review Broadway. Keep T2.

picksinsix.justification: PicksInSix appears to be a personal review feature on conversationswithedtracy.com with 6 reviews since 2025. Keep current T3.

pinkprincetheatre.justification: Unable to confirm what pinkprincetheatre.com is beyond a small London theatre review site active since July 2026. Keep current tier.

pioneer-press.justification: St. Paul Pioneer Press, a regional Minnesota daily reviewing touring productions. Matches T3 as a regional paper.

plays-international.justification: Plays International, a long-running UK theatre magazine with regular London coverage since late 2023 in the corpus. Matches T3.

plays-to-see.justification: Plays To See, a multi-contributor UK review site covering London and some NYC shows. Matches T3.

pop-dust.justification: Popdust, a pop culture site with incidental theatre coverage (5 reviews, 2017-2018). Keep current T3.

popbytes.justification: Popbytes, a celebrity and pop culture blog with incidental theatre coverage (5 reviews). Keep current T3 under the default-keep rule.

purewow.justification: PureWow, a lifestyle site with incidental theatre coverage (3 reviews). The current T4 fits.

queerty.justification: Queerty, an LGBTQ news site with regular theatre reviews 2022-2024. Keep T3.

rachelweinbergreviews.justification: Appears to be a personal theatre review site (5 reviews since late 2025). Keep current T3.

radio-times.justification: Radio Times, a national UK listings magazine whose theatre reviews are occasional but carry editorial oversight. Keep T3.

readaboutstuff.justification: readaboutstuff.com appears to be a small London review site with 33 reviews since December 2025; its editorial model is unclear. Keep current tier.

reflections-in-the-light.justification: Reflections in the Light, Lauren Yarger's Christian-perspective theatre blog, active in the corpus 2014-2018. Keep T3.

reviewing-the-drama.justification: Small theatre review site active 2015-2017 (defunct in the corpus). Keep current T3.

reviewsgate.justification: Reviewsgate was a long-running UK theatre review site whose critics included veteran reviewer Timothy Ramsden; the domain no longer hosts theatre reviews, so it is defunct. A multi-contributor site with established critics sits at T3, not the T4 blog floor; defunct outlets keep the tier that matched their standing.

revstanstheatreblog.justification: Rev Stan's Theatre Blog, a long-running single-author London theatre blog. Low volume; keep current T3.

rhombus-rota.justification: Unable to confirm what rhombusrota.co.uk is beyond a small UK review site with 6 reviews in 2026. Keep current tier.

rolandcat.justification: Single-author Substack newsletter with London reviews since June 2026. The current T4 fits.

rollingstone.justification: Rolling Stone, a major national magazine with occasional theatre reviews by staff writers. Keep T2.

san-diego-union-tribune.justification: San Diego Union-Tribune, a regional daily reviewing tours and transfers. Matches T3.

san-francisco-chronicle.justification: San Francisco Chronicle, a major regional daily with occasional reviews of NYC-bound shows. Keep T3.

san-jose-mercury-news.justification: San Jose Mercury News, a regional California daily reviewing tours. Matches T3.

scheckontheater.justification: Frank Scheck's personal review site; Scheck is a recognized critic (Hollywood Reporter, NYSR). Only 18 reviews in 2011 (inactive since); keep T3.

scribicide.justification: Scribicide, a small theatre review site active 2015-2019 (defunct in the corpus). Keep current T3.

seatplan.justification: SeatPlan, a theatre seating and ticketing site that publishes reviews; low volume and a commercial editorial model. Keep current T3.

show-showdown.justification: Show Showdown, a personal theatre blog active 2015-2019. Keep current T3.

showbiz411.justification: Showbiz411, Roger Friedman's entertainment news site with occasional theatre reviews, little activity since 2019. Keep current T3.

sierz-co-uk.justification: Personal site of Aleks Sierz, a recognized UK critic and author (Theatre Record, The Arts Desk). Keep T3.

simon-parris-man-in-chair.justification: Simon Parris: Man in Chair, an Australian single-author theatre blog with occasional NYC reviews 2015-2018. Keep current T3.

simon-seez.justification: Simon Seez, Simon Saltzman's blog; Saltzman is a long-time New Jersey theatre critic. Low volume 2016-2017; keep T3.

slantmagazine.justification: Slant Magazine, an established film and culture magazine with an editor and regular theatre reviews since 2016. Keep T2.

slate.justification: Slate, a national online magazine with very occasional theatre reviews. Keep T2 under the default-keep rule.

south-london.justification: southlondon.co.uk is a local news site from Community Matters Media Ltd (publisher of Southwark News and South London Weekly) that runs bylined theatre reviews. It is not the South London Press, which closed in 2025. A local news publisher with editorial oversight fits T3 rather than the T4 blog floor.

splash-magazines.justification: Splash Magazines, a multi-city lifestyle site with occasional theatre reviews. Keep current T3.

stage-left.justification: Stage Left, a NYC theatre review site active 2017-2019 (defunct in the corpus) with solid volume while active. Keep T3.

stageandcinema.justification: Stage and Cinema, a multi-contributor theatre site with an editor and rising 2022+ volume. Keep T3.

stagebuddy.justification: StageBuddy, a NYC theatre-specialist site with multiple contributors and sustained volume since 2015. Keep T3.

stagedtheatre.justification: Unable to confirm the editorial model of stagedtheatre.co.uk, a London review site active since June 2026. Keep current T4.

stagezine.justification: StageZine, a NY/NJ theatre site with notable 2015-2019 volume but almost none since 2022. Keep current T4; no clear evidence of higher standing.

standard.justification: Evening Standard, a London daily whose critics set the West End verdict; NYC coverage is negligible. Keep nyc2/lon1.

stu-on-broadway.justification: Stu on Broadway, a single-author Broadway blog active 2011-2018 (defunct in the corpus). Keep current T3.

susangrangercom.justification: Susan Granger's personal review site; Granger is a veteran film and theatre critic. Very low volume (2017); keep T3.

talkinbroadway.justification: Talkin' Broadway, a long-established theatre site with recognized regular critics and high sustained volume since 1997. Matches T2.

telegraph.justification: The Telegraph, a UK national daily whose critics set the London verdict; its NYC reviews are a secondary market. Keep nyc2/lon1.

the-clyde-fitch-report.justification: The Clyde Fitch Report, an arts and politics site with an editor and multiple contributors, active 2015-2017 in the corpus. Keep T3.

the-contending.justification: The Contending appears to be a small culture site with 20 NYC reviews since late 2024; editorial model unclear. Keep current T3.

the-cultural-critic.justification: The Cultural Critic, a small review site active 2016-2017 (defunct in the corpus). Keep current T3.

the-culture-mom.justification: Small lifestyle and culture blog with occasional Broadway reviews, 5 NYC reviews between 2016 and 2018 and no recent activity. Semi-pro tier fits; keep.

the-globe-and-mail.justification: Canada's national daily newspaper; its critics review Broadway only occasionally (6 NYC reviews). Its standing is high at home but it is not a regular voice on Broadway, so T3 is reasonable.

the-interested-bystander.justification: Small NYC theatre review site active since 2024 with 26 reviews. I cannot confirm its editorial model, so keep the current tier.

the-jewish-chronicle.justification: Long-running UK national Jewish weekly with a regular theatre critic; 24 London reviews since 2025. A niche-audience paper with a real critic fits T3.

the-jewish-voice-and-opinion.justification: Small community publication with incidental theatre coverage, 2 reviews total. T4 fits.

the-knockturnal.justification: NYC entertainment and lifestyle website with multiple contributors; only 6 reviews, all from 2026. Keep.

the-komisar-scoop.justification: Single-author site of journalist Lucy Komisar with 141 NYC reviews from 2007 to 2026 and sustained presence in both periods. Long-running and picked up by aggregators, so keep T3.

the-morning-star.justification: UK national left-wing daily with a small circulation and a regular arts section; 5 London reviews. T3 fits.

the-news-herald.justification: Local Ohio daily newspaper with occasional Broadway or touring coverage (6 reviews). Local paper, T3.

the-oakland-press.justification: Local Michigan daily newspaper; 5 reviews over four years. Local paper, T3.

the-queer-review.justification: Small LGBTQ culture review site with 3 reviews total. Keep T4.

the-recs.justification: Small recommendations and review site (therecs.co.uk) with 40 reviews since mid 2025, mostly on NYC shows. I cannot confirm its editorial model, so keep the current tier.

the-spectator-uk.justification: Long-established UK weekly magazine with a regular staff theatre critic; 52 London reviews. Major magazine fits T2.

the-spy-in-the-stalls.justification: Small London theatre blog that started in 2026 (23 reviews). Keep T4.

the-three-tomatoes.justification: Lifestyle website aimed at older women with occasional theatre reviews; 5 NYC reviews from 2015 to 2018, no recent activity. Keep.

theartsdispatch.justification: Substack newsletter with 9 reviews since 2026, mostly London. Likely single-author, but I cannot confirm who writes it, so keep the current tier.

theater-in-the-now.justification: Small NYC theatre site with 6 reviews, all from late 2015, apparently defunct. Keep the tier it held.

theater-life.justification: Long-running NYC theatre review site with 516 reviews from 2007 to 2026 and one of the highest steady shares of the NYC corpus in both periods. A regular, aggregator-recognized voice; keep T2.

theater-news-online.justification: NYC theatre news and review site, 34 reviews from 2014 to 2020, now inactive (likely defunct). Keep the tier it held.

theater-pizzazz.justification: TheaterPizzazz.com is a NYC theatre site founded 2012, run by an editor/publisher with about 18 contributing writers, including established critics such as Carol Rocamora and Samuel L. Leiter, and a named chief theatre critic (Ron Fassler, 2026). With 177 NYC reviews that is a multi-contributor site with an editor, so T3 fits better than the T4 blog floor.

theater-reviews-from-my-seat.justification: Small review site with 10 NYC reviews in 2018 and 2019, now inactive. Keep.

theater-scene.justification: Long-running NYC theatre review site with a stable of experienced critics; 436 reviews and rising share since 2022. Regular aggregator-recognized voice; keep T2.

theatermania.justification: Major theatre-specialist site with staff critics, 513 NYC reviews and one of the largest shares of the corpus. Standard T2 per the rubric.

theatre-bee-uk.justification: Small UK theatre review site with 5 London reviews in mid 2022 only. Keep.

theatre-is-easy.justification: Multi-contributor NYC theatre review site (theasy.com), 22 reviews from 2009 to 2015, inactive since. Keep the tier it held.

theatre-news.justification: Small UK theatre site with 2 reviews. Keep T4.

theatre-reviews-limited.justification: Long-running NYC theatre review site with 120 reviews from 2015 to 2026, steady presence. Semi-pro specialist site, keep T3.

theatre-south-east.justification: Regional UK theatre review site focused on the south east, 8 London reviews. Keep.

theatre-vibe.justification: Small UK theatre blog with 19 London reviews since 2024. Keep T4.

theatre-weekly.justification: Keep T2. Theatre Weekly is an active UK theatre news and review site with named bylines and a reviewer recruitment programme. A T3 move was considered on the belief that contributors are mostly volunteers, but that could not be verified (its about page returns 404), so no move is proposed.

theatreandtonic.justification: London theatre review site active since late 2024 with 67 London reviews. Small specialist site, keep T3.

theatreboard.justification: Small site (theatreboard.com) with 9 London reviews since June 2026. I cannot tell what this outlet is, so keep the current tier.

theatrecat.justification: Blog of Libby Purves, former chief theatre critic of The Times; 32 London reviews since 2023. Single-author, but a recognized critic, so T3 rather than T4.

theatrely.justification: NYC theatre site founded 2021 with a team of contributors and an editor; 196 reviews and a high share of the 2022+ corpus. Regular aggregator-recognized voice; keep T2.

theatres-leiter-side.justification: Single-author blog of theatre historian Samuel L. Leiter; 56 NYC reviews, mostly 2015 to 2019, last in 2022. Recognized critic, so keep T3.

thelivereview.justification: Small UK live entertainment review site, 6 London reviews since 2025. Keep.

thereviewshub.justification: Keep T2. The Reviews Hub (formerly Public Reviews, rebranded 2015) lists about 150 reviewers and 10 editors across UK regions plus New York, describing them as experienced journalists, theatre professionals and arts graduates. A T3 move was considered on the belief that reviewers are volunteers, but the site does not say so, so the move is not proposed.

thestage.justification: UK theatre trade paper of record with staff critics; 196 London reviews and 91 NYC reviews. Market-setting in London (T1), established trade outlet in NYC (T2); keep the split.

theupcoming.justification: London culture webzine with many unpaid contributors; 35 London reviews since 2025. Keep T4.

thewrap.justification: Hollywood trade and entertainment news site with a long-serving theatre critic; 388 NYC reviews and sustained share. T2 fits.

third-coast-review.justification: Chicago arts and culture site with occasional touring or NYC coverage, 6 reviews. Keep T3.

this-week-in-new-york.justification: NYC events newsletter (twi-ny.com) with largely single-author coverage; 57 reviews. Keep T4.

thisbroadsway.justification: Small Broadway site with 6 reviews from 2014 to 2018, inactive. Keep.

time.justification: National news magazine with a long-serving theatre critic; 10 NYC reviews, the last in 2014, so its theatre coverage is effectively defunct. Keep the T2 tier it held.

timeout.justification: Time Out New York has a highly regarded chief critic and a steady 498 NYC reviews, but it is a listings and culture magazine, and the rubric places Time Out at T2 alongside TheaterMania and NY Post, not with the NYT, Vulture, Variety tier. London tier unchanged (no London reviews). Considered NYC T1 to T2, not proposed: Time Out New York has a long-serving chief critic and is a leading NYC voice, so T1 stands.

timeout-london.justification: Time Out London is an established listings and culture magazine with staff critics and 174 London reviews, but the rubric's London T1 is the major national papers plus The Stage, and it lists Time Out at T2. NYC tier unchanged. Considered London T1 to T2, not proposed: Time Out London is a leading London theatre voice with an established chief critic, so T1 stands.

times-square-chronicles.justification: NYC theatre and nightlife site (t2conline.com) with 62 reviews and a promotional slant. Keep T4.

times-uk.justification: UK national daily with staff critics; 158 London reviews and 24 NYC reviews. Market-setting in London, established but secondary on Broadway; keep the split.

timesofsandiego.justification: Local San Diego news site with 6 reviews, likely of touring or pre-Broadway productions. Local outlet, T3.

toronto-star.justification: Major Canadian daily; only 5 Broadway reviews over 25 years. Not a regular Broadway voice; keep T3.

towleroad.justification: LGBTQ news blog that ran a regular theatre column from 2015 to 2019 (62 NYC reviews), now inactive. Keep the tier it held.

towncountry.justification: Town and Country, national lifestyle magazine with incidental theatre coverage; 6 reviews in 2016 and 2017. Keep T3.

uinterview.justification: Entertainment news and interview site with incidental theatre reviews, 5 reviews to 2019. Keep.

unmissabletheatre.justification: Small UK theatre review site, 8 London reviews since July 2026. Keep.

upstage-downstage.justification: Blogspot theatre blog with 7 NYC reviews from 2016 to 2019, inactive. Keep.

usatoday.justification: National daily with a long-serving theatre critic; 240 NYC reviews. Major daily fits T2.

variety.justification: Entertainment trade paper of record with staff critics; 612 NYC reviews and the largest share of the corpus. T1 in NYC; 13 London reviews where it is a secondary voice, keep T2.

viewfromthegods.justification: Small UK theatre review site, 7 London reviews in 2026. Keep.

village-voice.justification: Historic NYC alternative weekly with established critics; 113 reviews, mostly before its 2018 print closure, little since. Effectively defunct for theatre; keep the T2 it held.

vogue.justification: National fashion magazine with incidental theatre coverage, 6 reviews over ten years. Keep T3.

vox.justification: National news site whose staff critic occasionally reviewed Broadway; 9 reviews to 2023. Low volume, but staff critics at a major outlet; keep.

vulture.justification: New York magazine's culture site with a leading staff theatre critic; 524 NYC reviews. Market-setting on Broadway; keep.

w42st.justification: Hyperlocal Hell's Kitchen community site with 1 review. Keep T4.

washpost.justification: Major national daily with a long-serving chief theatre critic; 330 NYC reviews. Keep T1 in NYC.

west-end-best-friend.justification: London theatre blog with 83 reviews since 2023 and steady presence. Keep T3.

west-end-wilma.justification: London theatre blog with 23 reviews. Keep T4.

whatsonstage.justification: Established UK theatre-specialist site with professional critics; 162 London reviews. Standard T2 per the rubric.

wnyc.justification: New York public radio station with a regular theatre critic; 34 NYC reviews from 2016 to 2019, theatre reviews inactive since. Keep the T2 it held.

wolf-entertainment-guide.justification: Small entertainment review site with 37 NYC reviews from 2015 to 2019, inactive since. Keep.

wsj.justification: National daily with a long-serving staff drama critic; 450 NYC reviews. Market-setting on Broadway; keep.

yale-daily-news.justification: College student newspaper with 1 review. Keep T4.

zeal-nyc.justification: NYC lifestyle and culture site with 44 reviews from 2014 to 2018, inactive since. Keep the tier it held.
